memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"The deep waters have covered them; they sank to the depths like a stone. Your
right hand, LORD, was majestic in power. Your right hand, LORD, shattered the
enemy." - Ex 15:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Twice in one breath: "Your right hand, LORD." The song cannot say it once and
move on.

In Scripture, the right hand stands for strength and for action. It is the hand
that works, that fights, that saves. And here the poetry marvels that this hand
is both majestic and effective. It is not only impressive; it accomplished
something.

There is a quiet contrast running through these lines. Egypt's soldiers sank
"like a stone," heavy, helpless, going down. Israel walked through on dry
ground. Same water, opposite outcomes.

We should notice what the song does not say. It does not say Israel was strong.
It does not say they fought well. Every line of credit goes to God's right hand.

The New Testament picks up this image and takes it somewhere astonishing. Christ
is now seated "at the right hand of the Majesty in heaven" (Heb 1:3). The place
of power belongs to the One who was crucified. And Paul prays that believers
would grasp God's "incomparably great power for us who believe," the same power
that raised Christ from the dead (Eph 1:19-20).

The right hand that shattered Egypt is the hand that holds you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you relying on your own hand rather than God's?
2. Does the power that raised Christ feel real to you, or only theoretical?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, Your right hand is majestic in power. Help me to stop striving in my own
strength and rest in Yours. Amen.
